title: Descent of the Cohen--Macaulay locus of a groupoid saturation
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and let $(U,R,s,t,e,i,c)$ be a groupoid scheme over $S$ [def-a1-groupoid-scheme], all structure morphisms being over $S$. A morphism $f:X\to Y$ is Cohen--Macaulay at $x\in X$ if it is flat at $x$ (the local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{Y,f(x)}$) [def-weil-flat-morphism] and the local ring at $x$ of the scheme-theoretic fibre $X_{f(x)}$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] with depth [def-weil-pbc-depth] equal to Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. It is Cohen--Macaulay if this holds at every point. Assume $s,t$ are flat and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Let $g:B\to U$ be locally of finite presentation and put $H=B\times_{g,U,t}R$, $p=\operatorname{pr}_B:H\to B$, and $h=s\circ\operatorname{pr}_R:H\to U$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. There exists an open subscheme $W\subseteq B$ [def-weil-open-immersion] such that $p^{-1}(W)$ is exactly the set of points at which $h$ is Cohen--Macaulay, with its open subscheme structure. In particular $h|_{p^{-1}(W)}$ is Cohen--Macaulay and locally of finite presentation, and whenever $h$ is Cohen--Macaulay at $(b,e(g(b)))$, one has $b\in W$.

source.place: Tag 04LH (lemma-local-source) with Tag 047W (remark-local-source-apply), item (5): Q = locally of finite presentation, R = flat and locally of finite presentation, P = Cohen--Macaulay. Pointwise openness uses More on Morphisms, openness of flatness and Tag 045U (lemma-flat-finite-presentation-CM-open).

proof.text: By clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], $H\to R$ is locally of finite presentation, as the base change of $g$ along $t$. Composition with $s$ is locally of finite presentation by [lem-sbc-locally-finite-presentation-composition], so $h$ is locally of finite presentation. By [lem-sbc-restricted-fibre-locally-noetherian], with the whole target as its open, every fibre of $h$ is locally Noetherian.

Let $F\subset H$ be the points where $h$ is flat. Apply [lem-sfb-relative-flat-affine-charts] with its $S=Y=U$, $q=\mathrm{id}_U$, $p=f=h$. The identity is locally of finite type (on an affine it is generated as an algebra by the empty set), and $p$ is locally of finite presentation by step 1. The cited statement gives around every point an open affine chart on which $F$ is an open set $E$. Thus $F$ is open in $H$. The map $h|_F$ is flat by definition [def-weil-flat-morphism]. The inclusion $F\hookrightarrow H$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale]; clause (i) of [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-source-target-properties] gives local finite presentation of $h|_F$.

source.place: Tag 0399 (theorem-openness-flatness), structure-sheaf case; source restriction to the flat locus.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sbc-fibre-cohen-macaulay-locus-open] to the flat locally finitely presented map $h|_F$. It gives an open $D$ in $F$, hence in $H$, where the fibre local ring has depth equal to dimension. An open restriction leaves both source stalks and fibre stalks at its points unchanged [def-weil-open-immersion]. The fibres are locally Noetherian by step 1. Consequently $D$ is exactly the pointwise Cohen--Macaulay locus of $h$ as defined in the statement: membership requires flatness, hence membership in $F$, and then the displayed depth equality. In particular $h|_D$ is Cohen--Macaulay. The same source-restriction argument as step 2 gives local finite presentation of $h|_D$.

source.place: Tag 045U (lemma-flat-finite-presentation-CM-open), (1),(2), applied on the open flat locus; Tag 045R (definition-CM).

proof.text: We check the base-change rule needed below. For a locally finitely presented $f:X\to Y$ and a flat map $v:Y\prime\to Y$, write $f\prime:X\prime\to Y\prime$ for its base change and $a:X\prime\to X$ for the projection. At each $x\prime$, [lem-sfb-pointwise-flatness-base-change] gives flatness of $f\prime$ at $x\prime$ if and only if $f$ is flat at $a(x\prime)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-of-base-change], the new fibre is the old fibre extended from $\kappa(y)$ to $\kappa(y\prime)$. Each old fibre is locally finite type over $\kappa(y)$: tensoring an affine finite presentation $A[z_1,\ldots,z_n]/(q_1,\ldots,q_m)$ with $\kappa(y)$ gives the same finite presentation with reduced coefficients [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. The FIRST assertion of [lem-pur-cohen-macaulay-field-extension] therefore identifies the two fibre Cohen--Macaulay conditions at these points. It imposes no Noetherian condition on $Y$ or $Y\prime$. Combining the two equivalences gives: $f\prime$ is Cohen--Macaulay at $x\prime$ if and only if $f$ is Cohen--Macaulay at $a(x\prime)$.

Put $C=H\times_B H$, with projections $a,b:C\to H$. Its components are $(\beta,r_1,r_2)$ with $g\beta=tr_1=tr_2$. Define $d=c(i(r_1),r_2):C\to R$ using [def-a1-groupoid-scheme]. Then $td=ha$ and $sd=hb$. The morphism $(a,d):C\to H\times_{h,U,t}R$ has inverse $((\beta,r),v)\mapsto(\beta,r,c(r,v))$. The morphism $(b,d):C\to H\times_{h,U,s}R$ has inverse $((\beta,r),v)\mapsto(\beta,c(r,i(v)),r)$. All maps exist by the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product]: the indicated composability conditions hold, and the new arrows have target $g\beta$. The inverse identities follow from the groupoid laws; for instance $c(i(r),c(r,v))=v$ and $c(r,c(i(r),r_2))=r_2$, and the second pair uses $c(c(r_1,i(r_2)),r_2)=r_1$. Thus the square with top $d$, bottom $h$, left $a$, right $t$, and the square with top $d$, bottom $h$, left $b$, right $s$, are cartesian. This is an explicit verification from the two cited definitions, not an additional groupoid theorem.

source.place: Tag 04LH (lemma-local-source), second cartesian diagram; groupoids.tex Tag 03C6 (lemma-diagram-pull), explicit division inverses.

proof.text: Apply the equivalence proved in step 4 to the two cartesian squares of step 5, with original map $h$ and flat base maps $t$ and $s$. These are flat by hypothesis, and $h$ is locally of finite presentation by step 1. At each $z\in C$, the condition that $d$ is Cohen--Macaulay at $z$ is therefore equivalent both to $a(z)\in D$ and to $b(z)\in D$. Hence $a^{-1}D=b^{-1}D$. The identity laws give a section $\sigma:B\to H$, $\beta\mapsto(\beta,e(g\beta))$, of $p$. Set $W=\sigma^{-1}D$, open by continuity. By [def-pc-fibre-product], the pair $(\mathrm{id}_H,\sigma p)$ defines $j:H\to C$, since both components have the same composite to $B$. Pulling the equality back along $j$ gives $D=(\sigma p)^{-1}D=p^{-1}W$. The open-immersion definition [def-weil-open-immersion] upgrades this equality of open subsets to equality of their open subschemes.

source.place: Tag 04LH (lemma-local-source), equality of inverse-image loci and final identity-section argument.

proof.text: By steps 3 and 6, $h|_{p^{-1}W}=h|_D$ is Cohen--Macaulay and locally of finite presentation. If $h$ is Cohen--Macaulay at $(b,e(g(b)))=\sigma(b)$, then $\sigma(b)\in D$, whence $b\in\sigma^{-1}D=W$. This proves every clause, including the empty-source case, where $D$ and $W$ are empty.

lean.statement: theorem groupoid_cohenMacaulayLocus_descends {S U R B : Scheme.{u}} (s t : R ⟶ U) (e : U ⟶ R) (i : R ⟶ R) (c : pullback s t ⟶ R) (uS : U ⟶ S) (rS : R ⟶ S) (_hs : s ≫ uS = rS) (_ht : t ≫ uS = rS) (_he : e ≫ rS = uS) (_hi : i ≫ rS = rS) (_hc : c ≫ rS = pullback.fst s t ≫ rS) (hG : IsGroupoidScheme s t e i c) (g : B ⟶ U) [Flat s] [Flat t] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation s] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation t] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation g] : ∃ W : B.Opens, (∀ z : ↥(pullback g t : Scheme.{u}), z ∈ (pullback.fst g t ⁻¹ᵁ W) ↔ Scheme.Hom.IsCohenMacaulayAtPoint (pullback.snd g t ≫ s) z) ∧ Scheme.Hom.IsCohenMacaulay ((pullback.fst g t ⁻¹ᵁ W).ι ≫ (pullback.snd g t ≫ s)) ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation ((pullback.fst g t ⁻¹ᵁ W).ι ≫ (pullback.snd g t ≫ s)) ∧ ∀ b : B, Scheme.Hom.IsCohenMacaulayAtPoint (pullback.snd g t ≫ s) ((pullback.lift (𝟙 B) (g ≫ e) (by simp only [Category.id_comp, Category.assoc, hG.identity_target, Category.comp_id])) b) → b ∈ W
